increments.title: Direct Mode is keyed to two observable cases
increments.goal: The session's rules and the README stop offering a judgement call as the test for Direct Mode and offer an observable predicate instead, with the price of taking it wrongly written down and every new rule guarded by a case in the repository suite.
criteria: `rulebook.md` keys Direct Mode to two observable cases: writing the issue file costs more than the change itself, and the loop cannot be run.
`rulebook.md` sends every task outside those two cases to Issue Mode.

`rulebook.md` states what taking Direct Mode for a task outside those two cases costs: the loop would have cut it `direct` and put a reviewer on the diff, and the session gives it no reviewer and spends the run's most expensive context on it.
`rulebook.md` quotes, verbatim, the rationalisation that price counters.
`rulebook.md` offers "small or obvious" nowhere as the test for Direct Mode.

`rulebook.md` keeps the rest of the Direct Mode section as it stands: read the code, change the code and the tests, run them, commit, push, open the pull request, and hand a broad search to a subagent.
`rulebook.md` keeps the mode-picking rule as it stands, including that an unanswered mode question falls to Issue Mode.
`test-repo.sh` has a case that turns red when `GEMINI.md` and `rulebook.md` differ.
Each rule this adds to `rulebook.md` gets a case in `test-repo.sh` that turns red when that rule is removed.
The paragraph in `README.md` that names the two modes states the same predicate as `rulebook.md` and states no other test.

steps.label: decompose

rulings: Cut the issue as a single increment, because all twelve criteria describe one change to the mode rules — the rulebook's Direct Mode predicate, the README paragraph that restates it, and the suite cases that guard the new rules — and any split would land a rule with no test or a test with no rule; wrong costs one increment reviewed as a slightly larger diff instead of two.

Classified the increment `full` rather than `direct`, because the rule text and the verbatim rationalisation it quotes are still to be composed and the issue demands new `test-repo.sh` cases that do not exist; wrong costs one research and one test-author step the run could have skipped.
Listed GEMINI.md in the codemap although it is currently a symlink to rulebook.md, because two criteria turn on it and the researcher has to see it; wrong costs one line of the map.
return.summary: One increment: rulebook.md keys Direct Mode to the two observable cases (the issue file costs more than the change, and the loop cannot be run), sends everything else to Issue Mode, names the price of taking it wrongly with the rationalisation quoted verbatim, keeps the rest of the section and the mode-picking rule, and README.md plus test-repo.sh follow. Criterion map: rulebook keys two cases -> inc-1; everything else to Issue Mode -> inc-1; price stated -> inc-1; rationalisation quoted verbatim -> inc-1; 'small or obvious' gone -> inc-1; rest of Direct Mode kept -> inc-1; mode-picking rule kept -> inc-1; GEMINI.md byte-identical -> inc-1; test-repo.sh identity case -> inc-1; a case per added rule -> inc-1; README paragraph states the same predicate -> inc-1; `bash test.sh` exits 0 -> inc-1. Rejected splitting the rulebook rewrite from its suite cases, since a rule shipped without the case that turns red on its removal is exactly what the issue's last two criteria forbid, and rejected splitting README off, since its paragraph has to state the predicate the same edit invents.

steps.prompt:
Issue directory: docs/issues/2026-08-16-direct-mode-has-a-predicate
Open the run state for docs/issues/2026-08-16-direct-mode-has-a-predicate/issue.md: map the issue against the codebase, decide the cut, and write both into docs/issues/2026-08-16-direct-mode-has-a-predicate/backlog.json with the `init` subcommand of the backlog helper your shared brief names, with workflow "agile-loop" and the whole codemap in the payload's `codemap` field.
This run works at most 8 increments, so a cut that needs more than that is a cut that is too fine.
Announce this step before you begin it and record it before you return, the way your shared brief describes, with the backlog helper it names:
  - `start docs/issues/2026-08-16-direct-mode-has-a-predicate/backlog.json - decompose <the prompt file>` — the prompt you were given, verbatim and whole, in a file outside the repository.
  - `record docs/issues/2026-08-16-direct-mode-has-a-predicate/backlog.json - decompose <the return file> <the prompt file>` — your return, in a file outside the repository, with that same prompt file. Commit it with your work and push the commit.
The fields your return carries, and your page says what each one holds:
  - `questions`
  - `rulings`
  - `summary`
